acceptance_criteria.condition: The fresh v7 corpus contains exactly 20 new task IDs in the preregistered 6/8/6 strata; every buggy public suite fails and every reference public plus hidden suite passes.
The versioned v7 runner and scorer preserve the post-exit hidden-scoring boundary, and running the v7 entry point restores all delegated v6 module bindings afterward.
The v7 envelope freezes model, Harness, Skill, prompts, corpus, generator, v7/v6 runner and scorer hashes, task plan, seed, strata, and statistical thresholds before any trial.
The package remains regression-clean and statically typed after adding the v7 preparation protocol.

invariants: v7 does not reuse v6 hidden task trees or prior candidate outputs.
The preregistration remains status planned with an empty trials list and therefore cannot support an effect claim.
A v7 entry-point call cannot leave v6 model, Harness, or scorer bindings patched in a long-lived process.
Hidden tests and reference repairs are scorer-only and never enter the repair Agent workspace before process exit.
An incomplete v7 condition remains interrupted and ineligible; it is never selectively dropped, retried, or analyzed.

safeguards.name: fresh held-out corpus
safeguards.rationale: The v7 generator materializes 20 new IDs and the tests assert that historical v6 naming families are absent.

safeguards.name: blind post-exit hidden scoring
safeguards.rationale: The v7 scorer is a versioned entry point and the delegated scorer injects hidden tests only into a temporary copy after Agent exit.

safeguards.name: protocol hash envelope
safeguards.rationale: The preregistration locks all outcome-affecting inputs and its protocol and immutable-envelope digests are checked before collection.

safeguards.name: delegated binding restoration
safeguards.rationale: The v7 wrapper restores the v6 runner globals in a finally block; a dedicated in-process regression test catches cross-version contamination.

design_boundary.rationale: The generator owns fixture materialization, the v7 wrapper owns version selection and binding lifetime, the base runner owns execution/checkpoint state, and the scorer owns hidden-contract execution.

dependency_audit.rationale: No dependency, lockfile, or package manager change; the protocol uses existing Python standard-library and Codex CLI surfaces.

extension_decision.rationale: No application extension point or public adapter contract is introduced.

data_ownership.rationale: Public corpus files, hidden reference trees, preregistration, and future raw trial artifacts have distinct owners and lifecycle boundaries; hidden content is scorer-only.

error_model.rationale: Public failure, hidden failure, scope violation, timeout, nonzero Agent exit, binding contamination, and interrupted collection remain distinct outcomes.

contract_evolution.rationale: v7 is a new protocol envelope and held-out corpus; the historical v6 preregistration and interrupted result remain replayable and are not rebound to the corrected live wrapper.

operational_budget.rationale: The preregistered runner retains explicit Agent and scorer timeouts and fixed-pair stopping; the corpus tests execute all 20 public and reference hidden suites deterministically.

threat_boundary.rationale: The repair Agent receives only public task files and the optional Skill; hidden tests, references, prior outputs, and condition labels stay outside that input boundary. Native Codex isolation is protocol isolation, not a container security boundary.

delivery_lifecycle.rationale: The v7 corpus, wrappers, preregistration, tests, README note, and this evidence artifact are one atomic verified Git scope, committed only after checks and review.

release_recovery.rationale: This is an offline evaluation protocol and performs no production release or rollout.

data_migration.rationale: No application schema, persistence representation, backfill, or user data is changed.

configuration_secrets.rationale: Only non-secret model and Harness identifiers are preregistered; no credential, token, or secret is stored in source, prompts, or evidence.

dependency_supply_chain.rationale: No runtime or build dependency is added or updated.

operational_knowledge.rationale: README records v7's scope, interruption rule, isolation limitation, versioned entry points, and the exact not-run interpretation; the existing reference remains the hash-frozen general protocol.

reproducibility.rationale: The corpus manifest, source hashes, prompt hashes, v7/base runner and scorer hashes, analyzer hash, model, Harness, seed, task strata, and statistical stopping rule are frozen before collection.

It independently reran the v7 and full package tests, recomputed preregistration and supporting-artifact hashes, confirmed post-exit hidden scoring, and verified that no effect claim is made.

supporting_artifacts.summary: Normative Skill revision frozen as the treatment input.
Deterministic v7 generator for 20 held-out causal-repair tasks.
Frozen manifest with task strata, allowed edit paths, public/hidden tree hashes, and 20 task IDs.
Versioned v7 wrapper with scoped delegation and restoration of v6 bindings.
Corrected v6 execution/checkpoint implementation retained as a separately hashed dependency.
Underlying scorer implementation with post-exit hidden injection.
Planned v7 paired envelope with no trial records and verified protocol/envelope digests.
Contract tests for fresh task count, public failure, hidden reference success, and deterministic manifests.
Contract tests for version isolation, preregistration hashes, hidden boundary, and v6 binding restoration.
Blind paired analyzer whose planned-protocol output is not_run until complete trials exist.

remaining_risks: No v7 Agent condition has run; no Skill repair-success or causal-quality improvement claim is supported.
The synthetic v7 corpus covers selected owner, identity, boundary, retry, and integration contracts and cannot represent every production causal failure.
Native Codex workspace isolation remains protocol isolation rather than filesystem or container security isolation.
The completed paired run remains dependent on model-service availability; any incomplete condition must remain ineligible under the fixed protocol.
